headline: President of India to Grace NIFT Combined Convocation 2026 Tomorrow in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Textiles

President of India to Grace NIFT Combined Convocation 2026 Tomorrow in New Delhi

Combined Convocation to Bring Together Graduating Students from 18 NIFT Campuses Across the Country

30 AUG 2026 9:35AM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, the official Visitor of the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), will grace the NIFT Combined Convocation 2026 as the Chief Guest on 31 August 2026 in New Delhi, where graduating students from 18 NIFT campuses across the country will come together to celebrate the conferment of their degrees and mark the culmination of their academic journey at the Institute. The occasion will also recognize the academic excellence, creativity, dedication and achievements of the graduating students.

The Union Minister for Textiles, Shri Giriraj Singh, will also grace the occasion, along with other distinguished dignitaries, members of the Board of Governors, senior officials, faculty members, scholars and graduating students.

The Convocation will celebrate the achievements of NIFT’s graduating students and recognize their academic excellence, creativity, dedication and contributions during their years at the Institute. The ceremony will honour outstanding students of each Programme across campuses with the highest CGPA with a gold medal.

The Combined Convocation will be followed by campus-wise Degree Distribution Ceremonies, where graduating students will formally receive their degrees and mark their transition from academic life into the professional world.

Established in 1986 under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) is a statutory institute governed by the NIFT Act, 2006. Over the years, the Institute has emerged as a leading institution for fashion education, bringing together traditional arts and crafts, academic knowledge, design innovation, technology, creative thinking and industry engagement.

With 20 professionally managed campuses across the country, NIFT continues to foster an inclusive and dynamic learning environment, equipping young talent with knowledge, skills and creative capabilities to contribute to India’s fashion and creative industries.

The Combined Convocation 2026 will be a moment to celebrate a generation that has learned to transform ideas into possibilities and creativity into impact. As the graduates step beyond the Institute, they carry with them the confidence to shape new narratives, create meaningful solutions, and contribute to India’s evolving creative landscape. Their journey at NIFT may be reaching its ceremonial conclusion, but their journey of imagination, innovation, and excellence is only beginning.

The occasion will therefore stand as both a celebration of accomplishment and a launchpad for the future- honouring the achievements of the graduating students while looking ahead to the role they will play in shaping the fashion, design, and creative ecosystem of a new India. In their talent, enterprise, and vision lies the promise of a more creative, innovative, and globally connected Viksit Bharat.

Rooted in NIFT’s spirit of creativity and excellence, the graduating batch is poised to shape new narratives in India’s fashion and creative sectors. Their journey at the Institute concludes, but their journey of innovation and impact begins.

headline: Prime Minister's press statement during the joint press statement with the President of Uzbekistan
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister's press statement during the joint press statement with the President of Uzbekistan

30 AUG 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

Your Excellency, My Friend, Mister President,

दोनों देशों के delegates,

मीडिया के साथियों,

ताशकेंट में मेरे और मेरे delegation के जिस आत्मीयता से स्वागत हुआ, जिस गर्मजोशी से स्वागत हुआ इसके लिए मैं राष्ट्रपति जी और उज़्बेकिस्तान के जनता का ह्रदय से बहुत बहुत आभार व्यक्त करता हूँ।

उज़्बेकिस्तान की यह मेरी चौथी यात्रा है। यह हमारे संबंधों की निकटता, करीबी समन्वय और हमारी गहरी मित्रता को दर्शाता है।

पिछले लगभग एक दशक से मुझे राष्ट्रपति जी के साथ काम करने का सौभाग्य मिला है। इस दौरान मैं उन्हें दस से ज्यादा बार मिल चुका हूँ, मुझे मिलने का अवसर मिला है।

उनकी सकारात्मक और दूरदर्शी सोच, और निरंतर सीखते रहने की भावना वाकई बहुत ही प्रेरणादायक है। भारत के प्रति उनकी गहरी मित्रता और अटूट प्रतिबद्धता के लिए मैं उनका हार्दिक अभिनंदन करता हूँ।

Uzbekistan is at the heart of Central Asia, and at the heart of India’s engagement with the region.

भारत और उज़्बेकिस्तान की सोच और आकांक्षाओं में गहरी समानता है। “Yangi Uzbekistan” और “विकसित भारत 2047”, दोनों के केंद्र में youth, innovation, inclusive growth और modern technology हैं। इस साझा vision पर चलते हुए हम दोनों देशों के लोगों की भलाई के लिए काम कर रहे हैं।

इस वर्ष हमारी Strategic Partnership के 15 वर्ष पूरे हो रहे हैं। इस विशेष अवसर पर हमने संबंधों को Comprehensive Strategic Partnership का दर्जा देने का निर्णय लिया है। आज हमने हमारी साझेदारी के इस नए स्वरूप में तेज़ गति और ठोस परिणामों के साथ आगे बढ़ने का ambitious agenda तैयार किया है।

हमारा द्विपक्षीय व्यापार एक बिलियन डॉलर पार कर चुका है। अब हमने 2030 तक पाँच बिलियन डॉलर व्यापार का लक्ष्य रखा है। इसके लिए हम market access, connectivity, banking और payment से जुड़े विषयों पर व्यवस्थागत रूप से आगे बढ़ेंगे।

Infrastructure development में win-win सहयोग बढ़ाने के लिए हम मिलकर काम करेंगे। Digital Public Infrastructure, AI, critical minerals, clean energy, स्पेस और नूक्लीअर एनर्जी में सहयोग हमारे संबंधों को future-ready बना रहा है।

कृषि और स्वास्थ्य में हमारी ताकतें एक-दूसरे की पूरक हैं। उज़्बेकिस्तान के horticulture अनुभव और भारत की आधुनिक agricultural practices को जोड़कर हम दोनों देशों की खाद्य सुरक्षा में योगदान देंगे।

उज़्बेकिस्तान की medicinal herbs और भारत की आयुर्वेद एक्स्पर्टीज़ भी एक natural combination हैं। आज Traditional Medicine पर हुए समझौते से हमारे साझा प्रयासों को बल मिलेगा।

हमारा प्रयास है कि हमारी साझेदारी केवल दो राजधानियों तक सीमित न रहे। इसलिए हम अपने cities और states के बीच partnerships स्थापित करने जा रहे हैं। इन partnerships से urban management, industry, education, tourism और culture में direct connections निरंतर बढ़ते रहेंगे।

दोनों देशों के बीच करीबी रक्षा और सुरक्षा सहयोग हमारे गहरे आपसी विश्वास को दर्शाता है। आने वाले समय में हम दोनों देशों की defence industries के बीच direct linkages, co-production और co-development को बढ़ावा देंगे।

हमारा मानना है कि terrorism, extremism और separatism पूरे क्षेत्र के लिए गंभीर चुनौती हैं। इनके विरुद्ध zero tolerance हमारा साझा संकल्प रहा है, और आगे भी रहेगा।

हमारे संबंधों की सबसे गहरी जड़ें हमारी साझा विरासत में हैं। आज हमने इन्हें और मज़बूत बनाने पर विशेष बल दिया।

उज़्बेकिस्तान की Buddhist heritage sites के संरक्षण के लिए हम मिलकर काम करेंगे। दोनों देशों के युवाओं, विशेषकर students और professionals के बीच exchanges को बढ़ावा देना हमारी उच्च प्राथमिकता है। दोनों देशों के बीच टुरिज़म बढ़ाने के लिए आज Program of Cooperation पर सहमति बनी है। मुझे खुशी है कि उज़्बेकिस्तान में हिन्दी भाषा को promote करने के लिए आज हम Scholarships की घोषणा करने जा रहे हैं।

Sports भी हमारे सहयोग के महत्वपूर्ण आयाम के रूप में उभर रहा है। पिछले वर्ष गोवा में बीस वर्षीय Uzbek Grandmaster सिंदारोव ने FIDE World Cup जीता। अब नवंबर में उनका मुकाबला भारत के बीस वर्षीय chess champion गुकेश के साथ होने वाला है। एक बिसात पर जब ये दो युवा सितारे आमने-सामने होंगे, तो ज़ाहिर है- इस मुकाबले पर पूरी दुनिया की नज़र होगी। अगले महीने समरकन्द में होने जा रहे Chess Olympiad के लिए भी मैं बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं देता हूँ। आने वाले समय में कुराश और कबड्डी जैसे traditional games भी हमारी स्पोर्ट्स साझेदारी को नई ऊर्जा देंगे।

आज की चर्चा ने हमारे संबंधों के भविष्य की एक स्पष्ट दिशा तय की है।

A stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.

आपकी मित्रता और आज की सार्थक चर्चा के लिए एक बार फिर आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

दो दिन बाद उज़्बेकिस्तान अपनी स्वतंत्रता की 35वीं वर्षगांठ मनाएगा। मैं 140 करोड़ भारतवासियों की ओर से आपको और सभी नागरिकों को हार्दिक बधाई और शुभकामनाएँ देता हूँ।

बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

(Release ID: 2304701)

### OVERVIEW
The Prime Minister announced the elevation of India-Uzbekistan relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and outlined an ambitious agenda targeting $5 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 through enhanced cooperation across multiple sectors.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
*   **Date**: 30 August 2026.
*   **Partnership Status**: Both nations upgraded their relationship to a "Comprehensive Strategic Partnership" during a joint press statement with the President of Uzbekistan.
*   **Trade Targets**: Bilateral trade has exceeded $1 billion; the new goal is $5 billion by 2030.
*   **Cooperation Sectors**:
    *   **Technology & Innovation**: Focus on digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), critical minerals, clean energy, space, and nuclear energy.

    *   **Urban Development**: Establishment of partnerships between cities and states to improve urban management, industry, education, tourism, and culture.

*   **Cultural Heritage**: Joint efforts to protect Uzbek Buddhist heritage sites.
*   **People-to-People Ties**: Promotion of Hindi language in Uzbekistan via scholarships; increased youth exchanges and a formalized program of cooperation for students and professionals.
*   **Sports**: Agreement on a chess rivalry between Uzbek grandmaster Sindarov and Indian champion Gukesh; support for traditional games such as Kushand and Kabaddi.
*   **Strategic Vision**: The partnership is positioned as a powerful force for peace, progress, and prosperity in Central Asia.

headline: Vice President inaugurates Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali, celebrates Keralam’s rich cultural heritage
fullText:
Vice President's Secretariat

Vice President inaugurates Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali, celebrates Keralam’s rich cultural heritage

Aranmula Vallamkali reflects Keralam’s timeless traditions, devotion and spirit of togetherness: Vice President

Tradition and modernity can go hand in hand: Vice President at Aranmula Vallamkali; recalls Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi’

30 AUG 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today inaugurated the Aranmula Uthrittathi Vallamkali on the River Pamba, describing the festival as a glorious symbol of Keralam’s rich cultural heritage, devotion and timeless traditions.

The Vice President said the Aranmula Vallamkali,… pic.twitter.com/n2iuofS92w

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 30, 2026

Congratulating the people of Keralam on the State’s recent renaming, the Vice President recalled that, as Chairman of Rajya Sabha, he had the privilege of presiding over the passage of the State Renaming Bill during the recently concluded Session. He also conveyed his greetings on the occasion of Onam.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the Aranmula Vallamkali, associated with Onam and the sacred tradition of Vallasadya, showcases teamwork, discipline and sportsmanship, with beautifully decorated Palliyodams and more than a hundred oarsmen rowing in perfect rhythm.

Highlighting the spiritual significance of the River Pamba, he said it forms an integral part of the Sabarimala pilgrimage and represents faith, purification and spiritual surrender. Recalling his seven pilgrimages to Sabarimala, he shared that he considers his first visit to the shrine, shortly before his nomination as a Member of Parliament, particularly significant. He said he believes Lord Ayyappa’s blessings were instrumental in his subsequent electoral victory.

Referring to Aranmula’s heritage, the Vice President highlighted the ancient Sree Parthasarathy Temple and the renowned GI-tagged Aranmula Kannadi. Recalling the celebrations at the Vice-President’s Residence last year, he said he had gifted Aranmula Kannadi to the guests, who greatly appreciated its exquisite craftsmanship. He stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional arts, crafts and knowledge systems for future generations.

Observing that people working abroad also return to participate in such cherished traditions, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Aranmula demonstrates how cultural traditions continue to connect people with their roots.

Emphasising that tradition and modernity can go hand in hand, he recalled Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”. He said India’s diverse festivals reflect the country’s cultural unity and observed, “Our diversity is not a source of division; it is a source of our strength.”

The programme was attended by Governor of Keralam Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar;

Minister for Home Affairs Shri Ramesh Chennithala; Minister for Higher Education Shri Roji M. John; Minister for Water Resources Shri Mons Joseph; MP Shri Anto Antony; MLA, Aranmula, Shri Abhin Varkey, and other dignitaries.

headline: Dr. Jitendra Singh holds Interaction with the delegation of Armed Forces HQ Association; Discussions Focus on Promotions and Pending Service-Related Issues
fullText:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

Dr. Jitendra Singh holds Interaction with the delegation of Armed Forces HQ Association; Discussions Focus on Promotions and Pending Service-Related Issues

Union Minister Assures Delegation that Representations made by them Will be dealt in Consultation with Stakeholder Departments

Dr. Jitendra Singh Assures of Thorough Examination of Employee Concerns

30 AUG 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today held an interaction with a delegation of the Armed Forces HQ Association, during which various demands and service-related concerns of employees were discussed.

The delegation submitted a memorandum to the Minister and held detailed discussions on issues concerning career progression, promotions and pending service-related matters. The interaction provided an opportunity for the representatives to place their concerns before the Minister and discuss the issues in a constructive and positive atmosphere.

Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the delegation for coming forward to discuss the concerns of employees in a structured manner. He said that continuous and constructive dialogue with employee representatives is important for addressing genuine service-related concerns and for ensuring greater administrative efficiency.

The Minister assured the delegation that the demands and representations submitted by them would be thoroughly examined in consultation with the relevant stakeholder departments. He further assured that he would make his best efforts in the interest of employees, while ensuring that the concerns raised are considered through the appropriate administrative process.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised that a structured and continuous engagement with employee representatives enables the administration to better understand service-related concerns and work towards their appropriate resolution. He reiterated the importance of an open and responsive approach in dealing with employee representations and assured that the concerns raised by the Association would receive due consideration.

The representatives of the Armed Forces HQ Association appreciated Dr. Jitendra Singh and the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) for their continued engagement with employee representatives and for giving due consideration to issues concerning government employees. They particularly acknowledged the work undertaken by DoPT in recent years in addressing long-standing employee-related issues and in taking steps aimed at reducing stagnation and improving employee morale.

The delegation also expressed appreciation for the Minister's approach of providing an opportunity to employee representatives to directly discuss their concerns. The interaction reflected the importance of maintaining a continuous dialogue between the administration and employee associations so that service-related issues can be appropriately examined and addressed.

The meeting concluded on a positive note, with both sides engaging in a constructive discussion on employee-related matters. The Minister reiterated that the representations submitted by the Association would be examined with the concerned stakeholders for appropriate consideration and action.

headline: NEET-PG 2026 Successfully Conducted Nationwide with Robust Security and Real-Time Monitoring
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

NEET-PG 2026 Successfully Conducted Nationwide with Robust Security and Real-Time Monitoring

Examination held for 2.73 lakh candidates across 1,111 centres in 339 cities covering all 36 States/UTs; Over 2.65 lakh candidates appeared

Examination for 2,445 Candidates Affected by Technical Disruption at Sitapura Centres in Jaipur on 5th September 2026

30 AUG 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi

The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) successfully conducted the NEET-PG 2026 examination today, 30 August 2026, across the country with comprehensive logistical, technological, security and manpower arrangements to ensure a fair, secure and seamless examination process.

The examination was scheduled for 2,73,096 candidates at 1,111 examination centres across 339 cities, covering all 36 States and Union Territories. A total of 2,65,980 candidates appeared for the examination, with the examination successfully completed for approximately 2,63,535 candidates.

The nationwide examination was supported by extensive real-time monitoring and stringent security measures. A total of 2,527 faculty members were appointed as Independent Appraisers to oversee the conduct of the examination. In addition, more than 700 senior faculty members, including Deans, Directors, Medical Superintendents and senior professors, were deployed as Flying Squad members.

To strengthen coordination and monitoring, 16 NBEMS Regional Command Centres were made operational across the country.

The examination centres were also placed under live CCTV surveillance, which was continuously monitored from the NBEMS Command Centre at its Headquarters in Dwarka. A dedicated team of 190 personnel from NBEMS and TCS was deployed for real-time surveillance and monitoring.

At the dedicated Command Centre at NBEMS Headquarters, officials from NBEMS, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, BEL, ECIL and TCS maintained close and continuous oversight of the examination process throughout the day.

As part of measures to further strengthen examination security and prevent impersonation, Aadhaar-based authentication of candidates was successfully undertaken at examination centres. Government agencies extended their full support towards the secure and orderly conduct of the examination.

While the examination was successfully completed for the overwhelming majority of candidates nationwide, an unforeseen technical disruption occurred at iON Digital Zone iDZ Sitapura Centres, Jaipur, Rajasthan (TC Nos. 41682 and 41683), where the examination could not be completed for 2,445 candidates due to internal power supply issues at the test centres, attributable to M/s TCS Ltd., the examination conducting agency.

NBEMS has expressed regret for the inconvenience caused to the affected candidates. To ensure that all affected candidates are provided a fair and equitable opportunity to appear in NEET-PG 2026, examination for these 2,445 candidates will be conducted on 05 September 2026 (Saturday) at 03:00 PM in Jaipur, Rajasthan.

The successful conduct of the examination across 1,111 centres in 339 cities reflects the extensive coordination among examination authorities, medical institutions, faculty, security agencies, technology teams and other stakeholders involved in the nationwide exercise.

NBEMS appreciates the cooperation, patience and trust of the candidates and acknowledges the dedicated efforts of all personnel and institutions associated with the conduct of NEET-PG 2026.

Viksit Bharat means quality education for children, clean water for every household, opportunities for youth & an inclusive society: RM

30 AUG 2026 1:42PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath performed the Bhoomi Pujan for 14 development projects, including 02 projects being implemented in collaboration with the state government, worth over Rs 100 crore at Lucknow Cantonment in Uttar Pradesh on August 30, 2026. These projects are: Artificial Intelligence based Solid Waste Management Plant; Multi-Utility Sports Complex; Modern Crematorium; 1500 KL Underground Reservoir; Replacement of old/outlived water supply pipeline; Construction of 08 Tubewells with SCADA Automation; Overhead Tanks with SCADA; Special School for Differently Abled Children in Lucknow Cantt; Construction of Additional Classrooms & Toilet at RA Bazar Madhyamik Vidyalaya; Construction of Additional Classrooms & Toilet at Rainbow Model School; Multi-Level Robotic Car Parking & Commercial Complex; and Legacy Waste-Bio-Mining & Bio-Remediation.

The two projects being implemented in collaboration with the state government are: RA Bazar City Polyclinic and Mukhyamantri Abhyudaya Coaching Centre. Raksha Mantri and the UP Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath also listened to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s ‘Mann ki Baat’ programme along with around 4,000 people.

In his address, Raksha Mantri stated that the initiatives reflect a comprehensive effort to improve civic amenities, education, healthcare, sports facilities, sanitation, cleanliness, water supply and urban infrastructure in the Cantonment. “The development of Lucknow Cantonment is closely linked with the progress of Lucknow. Coordinated efforts by the Centre and the State can accelerate development and good governance,” he added.

Crediting the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Raksha Mantri asserted that India is moving forward with the resolve to become a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. He emphasised that Viksit Bharat does not merely mean grand projects and modern buildings; but also means children receiving quality education, clean water reaching every household, youth getting opportunities to play and showcase their talent, and a differently-abled child never feeling left behind by society. He reiterated the Government’s commitment towards ensuring that development directly improves the people’s quality of life.

Referring to the renaming of several markets in Lucknow Cantonment, Raksha Mantri stated that names associated with the British era have been replaced with those of prominent personalities of India's freedom struggle and national life. Royal Artillery Bazar has been renamed Ekta Bazar, British Cavalry Bazar as Uda Devi Bazar, British Infantry Bazar as Matadin Valmiki Bazar and another British Infantry Bazar as Mangal Pandey Bazar, while Kanedy Market has been renamed Atal Bihari Vajpayee Market. He also called for a balanced approach to development and environmental concerns, stressing that genuine problems must be addressed through practical solutions rather than politicising every issue or opposing development by default. headline: English rendering of PM’s address in the 137th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 30.08.2026
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

English rendering of PM’s address in the 137th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 30.08.2026

30 AUG 2026 11:36AM by PIB Delhi

My dear countrymen, Namaskar!

I welcome you all once again to this new episode of ‘Mann Ki Baat’. All of you know that this is a platform where we bring to the fore new initiatives and discuss the innovative ideas of our fellow countrymen. Many of these ideas are the result of people investing their boundless energy into them.

Some time ago, someone wrote on social media, “On the auspicious occasion of Ashadhi Ekadashi, I am delighted to announce the launch of my initiative to make history interesting.” They further explained that the idea is quite simple: visit the website and select any year. There you can easily find out which ruler ruled over what part of India at that time. I found this quite interesting too and thought of learning more about it. I discovered that this work has been done by Shriman Krishna Seshadri, a resident of Mumbai. Interestingly, Krishna ji has kept the website’s name very simple: www.bharatrajya.com. The effort he has put in should reach all of you; that is why I thought, why not speak directly to Shri Krishna ji!

Krishna ji is joining us on the phone.

Prime Minister: Namaste, Krishna ji.

Krishna Seshadri: Namaste, Sir, Namaste.

Prime Minister: My friend, I’ve learned that you neither belong to the tech world nor are you a history teacher; yet, you utilized technology to create a website dedicated to history. I am very curious—how did this all come about?

Krishna Seshadri: Thank you, Sir; it is a great privilege to speak with you. To tell you a little about myself: I was an engineer, then I pursued an MBA and entered the field of marketing. However, throughout all this, I maintained a deep interest in history - something I’ve had since childhood. So, I always wanted to do something on history - how to make it interesting and I felt there was immense scope for improvement and change in how we teach history… we could present history to reach people as a story.

Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, what aspect of Indian history did you feel needed to be known by the maximum number of people?

Krishna Seshadri: Sir, the way Indian history is taught in our schools and colleges often focuses on the perspective of a single empire or kingdom, with those specific empires receiving disproportionate attention. Consequently, we remain unaware of many other great empires—such as the Cholas, the Pallavas, the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir, or the Ahoms, who preserved their culture and value system in Assam for at least 600 years. So, I decided to create a site that introduces people to these great empires.

Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, you work so hard; let me ask you a hypothetical question. If you had the opportunity to converse with any three figures from Indian history, who would you choose, and why?

Krishna Seshadri: Yes, Sir. First, I would speak to Rajaraja Chola or Rajendra Chola - who was one of the most powerful and significant kings of the Chola Empire Sir. So, I would want to understand the vision behind the establishment of massive Shiva temples like the Brihadisvara Temple or Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Where did that vision and planning come from? How did the thought occur to them to create something that would inspire people for the next one or two thousand years? So, that is what I would like to know from them. And, the second personality - who, in my opinion, is a highly underrated personality in Indian history - Sir, his name is Hemu. We usually read only two or three lines about him in Indian history.

Krishna Seshadri: We often don’t know the fact that Hemu was a common man - an ordinary individual and a merchant - who went on to build an empire; he was not just an empire-builder but also a military thinker and a military genius who fought 23 battles in his career and won 22 of them. I am very interested in understanding his thought process and the journey that took him from being an ordinary man to such a great king, Sir. The third figure is a very interesting personality - a woman named Tribhuvan Mahadevi. Her story belongs to the Bhaumakara dynasty of Odisha. Around 850 AD, the neighbouring Pala Empire invaded her kingdom, and her husband - the king - was martyred in the battle. Consequently, the empire shrank, and chieftains and leaders began abandoning it; however, Tribhuvan Mahadevi took charge of the administration. She became one of the first independent rulers in Indian history. She not only stabilized the government but also made it powerful enough to rule over Kalinga and the surrounding region for the next hundred years. So, these are the three interesting historical personalities I would like to meet, Sir.

Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, it seems like you are re-living history now; you’ve been completely immersed in it. See, I have also viewed your site with great interest, and what I found most fascinating was the tab allowing people to submit corrections and suggestions. Being open to such constructive feedback is a significant thing in itself.

Have you started receiving suggestions from people? And how do you act upon them?

Krishna Seshadri: Yes, Sir, we receive many suggestions from people. Suggestions generally fall into two categories. One type involves suggesting corrections - such as pointing out which king ruled a specific region or nation at a particular time, or clarifying when a specific battle took place. We receive other suggestions - such as adding specific features to the website - and we consider them all. For instance, if someone suggests that a particular king ruled a specific region during a certain era, we take that suggestion and cross-reference it with our sources. Someone suggested to us that while we had showcased India as a whole, it would be even better to display information similarly at the regional level; so, we implemented that feature. And then another suggestion led us to create a 'trump card' style feature - compiling data and statistics for various empires - to make the content more engaging for children. Someone also suggested consolidating these resources so they could be easily downloaded and shared, a feature we are currently implementing. It’s important for us to know that we are bound to make mistakes - we aren't the best. That is precisely why we consciously included a 'correction' tab; we want this to be a collaborative platform where contributions help us build a site that makes history an enjoyable subject for years to come.

Prime Minister: Krishna-ji, you have truly accomplished something remarkable. Okay, apart from history, you must be having a lot of other hobbies… or do you engage in other activities as well!

Krishna Seshadri: Well, actually, Sir, I’m a bit of a boring person.

Prime Minister: (Laughs)

Krishna Seshadri: I’m deeply interested in technology and history, and now that the two have come together, I spend my entire day immersed in that.

Prime Minister: Well, Krishna ji, I extend my very best wishes to you. You have made a good start, and your approach is such that people will connect with it - I am fully confident of that. My best wishes are with you.

This initiative by Krishna ji will help not only history students but all of us to learn about our past in an engaging way. If you also have information about such initiatives, please do share it.

My dear countrymen,

The 'Nasha-mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat' campaign is currently gaining momentum rapidly across the country. Its goal is absolutely clear: drug-free youth; a drug-free India.

I am happy that this campaign has not remained merely a formality; many people - especially our youth - are becoming a part of it in large numbers. After all, this is our collective resolve for the health, happiness, and bright future of India's youth.

Drug addiction does not just engulf a single individual; the entire family and society have to bear the consequences. I would like to commend those who raise awareness against drugs and step forward to help individuals struggling with addiction. Can you come up with a powerful slogan for a drug-free India? Can our young musicians create songs that convey the message of a drug-free life? Can students and theatre groups write touching short plays that highlight the dangers of drugs while also showing the path to recovery? Our country has no shortage of excellent content creators. I urge them to create content in various languages ​​that helps society in this endeavor. You can use your creativity as a medium for social change. Do share your efforts on social media using the relevant hashtag. Often, creative efforts prove more impactful than formal campaigns. Let us all play our part in this noble mission to keep India's youth away from drugs and free from addiction. Do share your efforts on social media with the hashtag #NashaMuktYuva

The month of August brings with it myriad hues of patriotism all around. During this time, the spirit of love for the nation intensifies in everyone's heart. Occasions such as 'National Handloom Day' and the anniversary of the 'Quit India Movement' to 'Partition Horrors Remembrance Day' make this month special. 'Independence Day' and 'National Space Day' fill every countryman with pride. The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign further strengthens this sentiment. This year has become even more special as it marks the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram'. This time, over 8 crore 'Tiranga selfies' were uploaded.

And this celebration of the Tricolour was not limited to India alone; this year, through the 'Suryapath Tiranga' initiative, our flag embarked on a unique journey across the globe. The Tricolour was hoisted in Suva, Fiji, at the first light of dawn. Subsequently, it was unfurled at Indian Missions and Posts across Asia, Africa, Europe, and eventually San Francisco in America. You can imagine how magnificent those scenes must have been; as the sun traversed across the world, the Indian Tricolour was hoisted in its wake. Such efforts bind society together and deepen our connection with the nation. I extend my heartiest congratulations to everyone involved in these initiatives.

From morning till evening, lakhs of women across the streets of our cities and towns are engaged in their work. Some sell vegetables or fruits, others run tea stalls, while some sell flowers, earthen lamps, and worship materials. Often, a mere lack of capital prevents their businesses from growing further. But now, lakhs of such mothers and sisters are gaining new strength through the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. This aspect of ‘women empowerment’ is not discussed as much as it should be. Women account for approximately 46 percent of the beneficiaries of the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. This means that around 35 lakh women across the country are expanding their businesses by connecting with this scheme.

Babita Sharma ji from Ghaziabad is an excellent example of this. Babita ji used to run a small stall selling items for worship - such as flowers, earthen lamps, incense sticks, and coconuts - thereby contributing to her family's livelihood. She worked very hard, but capital was needed to grow the business. She received financial assistance through ‘PM SVANidhi’. She increased her stock and expanded her business. Her customer base and income grew, and gradually, her small roadside stall transformed into a proper shop.

The story of T.S. Ningamma ji from Bengaluru is also very inspiring. Ningamma ji and her husband started a small venture selling idli, dosa, and sambar. The business took off, but capital was required to take it to the next level.

Ningamma ji also received support from ‘PM SVANidhi’. She upgraded her cart, began purchasing supplies in bulk, and added new items to her menu. As customers and earnings increased, the family's financial situation improved. Today, she is able to provide a better education for her three children.

When a woman's business grows, the future of her entire family advances along with it. Children receive a better education, household needs are met, and the woman's self-confidence is strengthened. This is, indeed, a living example of ‘women's empowerment.’ I extend my best wishes for a bright future to all the sisters involved in street vending.

Cleanliness has a remarkable quality. When the resolve to keep a place clean becomes the people's own commitment, the transformation is not limited merely to tidiness; it completely changes the identity of that place. Such efforts towards cleanliness in various parts of the country constantly inspire us. There is a village named Patwai in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. Two friends there, Akash and Rohan, noticed that their local area had become littered with filth. That was all it took; Akash and Rohan picked up garbage bags and set out to clean the area. Gradually, other young people joined them, and a team was formed - named ‘Clean-up Patwai.’ These youths have cleaned four Ganga ghats so far and removed over a tonne of plastic waste. They have also cleaned numerous ponds and public spaces.

Similar inspiring scenes of cleanliness and public participation were witnessed during the recent Shri Amarnath Ji Yatra. Thousands of sanitation workers toiled day and night to serve pilgrims along the arduous routes. During this year's pilgrimage, more than 400 metric tonnes of waste were collected and processed. There was one aspect of this effort that I particularly appreciated: pilgrims themselves became active participants in this cleanliness drive. Over 16,000 pilgrims took a pledge for cleanliness; more than 10,000 were awarded the ‘Responsible Yatri’ certificate. A unique experiment also took place here: dung from the horses and mules used during the pilgrimage was converted into biogas, and this clean energy was used to light the ‘Swachh Jyot’. In essence, cleanliness became a form of service and faith during this holy pilgrimage to Baba Barfani.

Whether it is our villages or cities, our rivers or pilgrimage sites—their identity is shaped by our conduct. And when cleanliness becomes a part of that conduct, the beauty of the place is further enhanced.

Sometimes a small hobby opens the door to great possibilities in life. The journey of Vesalu Puro from the Phek district of Nagaland is a case in point. Vesalu ji grew up in a farming family; she had watched her parents farm since childhood and had a deep love for flowers. In 2021, she began cultivating flowers on a small scale, driven by this very passion.

Gradually, she began to see a possibility in it. She observed that there was a constant demand for flowers, whether for weddings or other festivals. Vesalu decided to take her hobby further. Along the way, she received training in scientific flower cultivation from the local Krishi Vigyan Kendra. Then she planted thousands of gladiolus bulbs on just a quarter-acre of land. In her very first attempt, over 5,000 flowers bloomed. Friends, this success marked a new beginning for Vesalu. She took her flower cultivation efforts further. Flowers that once remained confined to local markets are now traveling from Nagaland to cities like Delhi and Mumbai. Vesalu Puro ji’s journey demonstrates that when a passion is combined with hard work and proper guidance, it can pave the way for new possibilities.

There are many people around us who initiate a small effort, and by and by, that effort transforms the lives of countless others. There is a village named ‘Dhodrokusum’ in the Debrigarh region of Odisha. Until a few years ago, Maithili Bhue ji from this village would visit the forest almost daily—sometimes to gather firewood, at other times to collect Mahua flowers and Kendu leaves, or to harvest bamboo shoots and other forest produce. The forest met many of the needs of her family and numerous others in the area; however, Maithili ji then became associated with Debrigarh Eco-Tourism. This marked a shift in her relationship with the forest, taking it towards a new direction.

Forest conservation now became a means of livelihood for her. Friends, this transformation in Maithili ji’s life inspired other women as well. Today, more than 60 women are actively involved in forest conservation. Some have taken up the responsibility of protecting wildlife, others are engaged in developing grasslands, and some are contributing to eco-tourism activities.

Maithili-ji and these sisters from Debrigarh have demonstrated that it is possible to protect nature while also achieving prosperity in life. The efforts of all these sisters serve as a great inspiration for all of us.

Today the flight of our daughters' dreams is soaring from the earth to outer space. And you will be proud to know that India is bringing together thousands of daughters who are nurturing such dreams, from across the globe. This initiative is named ‘Mission ShaktiSAT.’ Through it, 12,000 girl students from 108 countries are getting the opportunity to learn satellite technology and to advance in the field of innovation. On August 23rd - National Space Day - a wonderful glimpse of this mission was seen in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. The second phase of Mission ShaktiSAT was launched at the Gautam Buddha University. On this occasion, around 100 female students from India and various other countries came together. Students selected from India's remote regions are also participating.

The goal of this entire initiative is truly special: preparations are underway to send a satellite - developed entirely through the participation of female students - into lunar orbit. Friends, I am confident that many of these students will carve out a distinct identity for themselves in the fields of science, technology, and innovation in the future.

The avocado fruit is creating quite a buzz these days. Hardly anyone knew about this fruit in the past; both its value and demand were low, but today it is frequently seen on dining tables. It has become a preferred choice in the health and premium markets. This is also very helpful for our farmer brothers and sisters. There’s an example of Varadaraj ji from Kadappa in Andhra Pradesh. He had been cultivating tomatoes and bananas on his farm for years. One day, he saw an avocado crop at a friend's farm. Subsequently, he gathered information about it on YouTube. So far, he has produced nearly 4 tonnes of avocados. Today, he supplies them directly to local shops. The new crop, scientific advice, and direct marketing have completely transformed the earnings from his small farm. Chandrashekharan ji, a farmer from Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu, started growing avocados on half a hectare of land. That is fetching him good prices, and his income has increased. In Chikkamagaluru, Karnataka, some farmer brothers and sisters have even planted avocados amidst their coffee plantations.

This allows them to earn additional income alongside coffee and black pepper. Friends, we often hear about the avocado toast in city restaurants, but through this very avocado, our innovative farmers have discovered a new recipe for earning. In other words, the avocado from our own country has enhanced the taste of your toast while simultaneously boosting the farmers' income.

In just a few days, on September 3rd, we will celebrate the birth centenary of the legendary Uttam Kumar. Friends, Uttam Kumar was a versatile actor who became deeply embedded in people's hearts through his acting. Film lovers believe that Satyajit Ray wrote the entire script for the film *Nayak* (The Hero) with Mahanayak Uttam Kumar in mind. Shriman Satyajit Ray had remarked that he possessed remarkable emotional depth alongside great dignity. He worked very hard to bring his characters to life. Uttam Kumar-ji was known not only for his natural ease but also for his philanthropy. His life offers another great lesson: never give up. Although his early films did not fare well, he remained focused on his work. It was this dedication that enabled him to reach such great heights. Friends, I recall passing by Uttam Kumar-ji’s house while doing a roadshow in Kolkata. Someone there even gifted me a photograph of him. I once again pay tribute to the legendary Uttam Kumar-ji; he will forever reign in our hearts.

“Mahanayak Uttam Kumar cheerodin maanusher hridaye Raj Korben”

Our festivals and celebrations not only uphold our traditions but also provide us with opportunities to connect with one another. In the coming days, we are set to celebrate several more significant festivals. The holy festival of Janmashtami falls on September 4th. We will also celebrate Vishwakarma Puja in September. On this occasion, we should honor the artisans, craftspeople, and Vishwakarma friends in our communities. Deepawali is also approaching in a few months, and preparations for it are already gradually underway. During this festive season, I once again urge you to be ‘Vocal for Local.’ Being ‘Vocal for Local’ does not merely mean buying earthen lamps; the vision behind it is much broader.

Whatever item we purchase for our homes, do ensure to see that it is made in India. The path to India becoming self-reliant will be paved only by taking pride in products made in India. It is also our responsibility to convey this message to as many people as possible. Our friends from the creative world, influencers, and celebrities also have a significant role to play in that. I urge you to personally embrace the 'Vocal for Local' spirit and inspire others to do the same.

There must be many people around you who are bringing about significant change in society through their small yet impactful efforts. Do write about them for 'Mann Ki Baat'. The experiences you share could become a source of new inspiration for someone, somewhere in the country. I look forward to your suggestions and experiences.

Thank you very much.

headline: Department of Consumer Affairs Notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

Department of Consumer Affairs Notifies Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026

Rules to establish Indian Standard Time as common time reference across the country

Rules to come into force after 180 days

30 AUG 2026 11:27AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Consumer Affairs has notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 on 27 August 2026. The Rules will come into force 180 days from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

The Rules provide for Indian Standard Time (IST) as the common time reference across the country for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes. The 180-day period will allow Government departments, businesses, institutions and other organisations to make the required changes to their systems before the Rules come into force.

The need for a common time reference has increased with the growing use of digital and technology-based systems. Banking and digital payments, telecommunications, railways, power systems, computer networks and government records depend on accurate time and time stamps. Differences between time sources can affect the coordination and recording of such activities. The Rules are aimed at ensuring that important systems across the country use accurate and consistent Indian Standard Time.

The common time reference will support:

accurate time-stamping of banking and digital payment transactions;

coordination of railways, airports and other transport systems;

reliable operation of telecommunication and internet networks;

accurate time-keeping in power systems;

maintenance of government and legal records; and

coordination of emergency and other time-sensitive services.

Use of Indian Timing Sources

The Government is developing infrastructure to disseminate accurate Indian Standard Time across the country through Indian institutions and Legal Metrology laboratories. The Rules also provide for the use of NavIC, India's satellite navigation system, and other approved Indian timing sources for reliable and secure time dissemination.

At present, several systems use foreign satellite-based time sources. The development of an Indian time dissemination infrastructure will provide additional options for critical systems and reduce dependence on external time sources.

White Rabbit Technology Demonstration

As part of the ‘One Nation, One Time’ initiative, a White Rabbit Technology-based Indian Standard Time Dissemination Demonstration Network was commissioned at the Regional Reference Standard Laboratory (RRSL), Bengaluru, in July 2026.

The system has demonstrated the dissemination of Indian Standard Time for sectors including banking, telecommunications, power, transportation and digital governance. The Department has also demonstrated secure dissemination of IST between RRSL Bengaluru and NSE Chennai, in collaboration with CSIR-NPL, ISRO, SEBI, NSE, BSNL and other stakeholders.

The 180-day period before commencement of the Rules will provide stakeholders time to review their existing systems, undertake necessary technical changes and prepare for implementation.The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 will provide a common Indian Standard Time reference for time-dependent systems and official purposes across the country.

headline: Hon’ble Vice President of India to Release “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Hon’ble Vice President of India to Release “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development

Major Thrust to Sustainably Harness the Untapped Potential of Island Resources

30 AUG 2026 11:13AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government of India is organizing an Outreach Programme of Ministry of Fisheries, Govt. of India at Agatti, Lakshadweep on Monday, 31st August 2026. The Hon’ble Vice President will Release “Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development.

The Outreach Programme will be graced by the august presence of Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj; Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, Hon’ble Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying and Panchayati Raj along with Shri Praful Khode Patel, Hon’ble Administrator of Lakshadweep. The event will also witness the participation of ssss fish farmers and fishers including women fish farmers and fishers in person, along with officials from the Department of Fisheries, GoI, Government of Lakshadweep, representatives from fisheries cluster and line Ministries and Departments.

India’s vast marine resources remain significantly underutilized despite the country’s immense oceanic wealth. With a coastline spanning 11,099 km, an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of 2.2 million sq. km and an estimated marine fisheries potential of 5.31 million tonnes, India possesses tremendous opportunities for sustainable fisheries, deep-sea fishing, mariculture and blue economy development. Lakshadweep exemplifies this untapped potential, with an EEZ of nearly 4 lakh sq. km, accounting for about 17% of India’s total EEZ, and a lagoon area of over 4,200 sq. km. This vast and resource-rich marine ecosystem offers significant scope for harnessing high-value fisheries resources, expanding mariculture, generating coastal livelihoods and accelerating sustainable blue economy growth.

The Government of India is adopting a cluster-based approach to drive integrated and value chain-oriented growth in the fisheries sector. In line with this strategy, Lakshadweep has been notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to promote cultivation, processing, value addition and market linkages. The Lakshadweep islands are also endowed with abundant marine ornamental fisheries resources, offering significant potential for sustainable rearing, exports and livelihood generation while conserving the marine ecosystems.

During the outreach program, The Hon’ble Vice President will distribute benefits to beneficiaries in fisheries sector and release the Mission Rangeen Machhli 2031” Strategic Action Plan for Ornamental Fisheries Development. The Strategic Action Plan will provide a uniform framework for scientific management, biosecurity, quality assurance and regulatory compliance across the ornamental fisheries value chain. The SOPs will standardize practices relating to broodstock management, breeding, hatchery operations, production systems, quarantine, health management, traceability, aquarium operations, handling, transport and trade, ensuring consistency and adoption of best management practices nationwide. They will also strengthen stakeholder capacities, improve product quality and biosecurity standards, facilitate certification and market access, and support the sustainable, organized and globally competitive growth of India’s ornamental fisheries sector.

India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of about 24 lakh sq. km. The marine fisheries potential within India’s EEZ is estimated at 58.6 lakh MT, supporting the livelihoods of approximately 50 lakh fishers and contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export revenues. India is presently among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing countries globally and exported seafood valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26.

Most fishing activities are concentrated within 40–50 nautical miles of the coast, while deeper waters and areas beyond national jurisdiction offer substantial opportunities for harvesting high-value species, particularly tuna and tuna-like resources. recognising the strategic importance of sustainable marine fisheries, the Government of India, has notified enabling framework for sustainable harnessing of fisheries from the Indian EEZ and the High Seas including Guidelines for Sustainable Harnessing of Fisheries in the High Seas by Indian-Flagged Fishing Vessels, 2025.

Lakshadweep is endowed with rich oceanic fisheries resources, particularly high-value tuna species such as Yellowfin Tuna and Skipjack Tuna, which form the backbone of the island’s marine fisheries sector. Supported by vast and productive waters, these commercially important species offer significant opportunities for sustainable harvesting, value addition, export growth and livelihood generation, positioning Lakshadweep as a key hub for tuna-based fisheries and blue economy development.

India–Chile CEPA Negotiations Advance; Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal Meets Chilean Vice-Minister Paula Estévez Weinstein

India–Chile CEPA to Deepen Trade and Investment Ties; Negotiations Targeted for Conclusion by Year-End

30 AUG 2026 10:51AM by PIB Delhi

Commerce Secretary Shri Rajesh Agrawal met Ms. Paula Estévez Weinstein, Vice-Minister of International Economic Relations of the Republic of Chile, on 26 August 2026 in Santiago, Chile, to advance negotiations on the India–Chile Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).

India reiterated its commitment to openness, sustained engagement and a balanced approach in strengthening the India–Chile economic partnership, with a focus on creating meaningful opportunities for businesses and people in both countries. The shared identity of India and Chile as members of the Global South, along with their common strategic vision, provides a strong foundation for deepening bilateral economic cooperation and advancing shared prosperity.

Both sides emphasised the importance of building on the strong and growing India–Chile relationship and ensuring that the CEPA translates shared objectives and aspirations into concrete and commercially meaningful opportunities for businesses on both sides.

The Commerce Secretary highlighted the immense potential for enhanced economic cooperation in sectors including healthcare, pharmaceuticals, energy, minerals, agriculture, machinery and engineering. The successful conclusion of the CEPA negotiations would provide further momentum to the growing bilateral trade and economic partnership between the two countries.

India remains committed to concluding the CEPA negotiations within this year, with the aim of delivering a balanced and mutually beneficial framework that provides equitable and commercially meaningful outcomes for businesses on both sides.

The CEPA is expected to open new avenues for greater trade and investment, while fostering cooperation in technology, talent and resilient supply chains, thereby creating stronger foundations for long-term economic cooperation between India and Chile.

headline: India's Higher Education Sector
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

India's Higher Education Sector

A Decade of Growth, Access, and Inclusion

30 AUG 2026 10:15AM by PIB Delhi

Building India’s Knowledge Ecosystem: A Decade of Progress

Higher education is a cornerstone of India’s journey towards a knowledge-based economy and a key pillar of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. The policy envisions an education system that promotes holistic, multidisciplinary learning and advances the goals of SDG 4. Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 focuses on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all. The Ministry of Education conducts an annual survey of Higher Education Institutions in India.

The All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), conducted annually by the Ministry of Education, provides a comprehensive evidence base on Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) across the country. The data helps track the progress of higher education reforms under NEP 2020, identify emerging gaps, and inform policy responses.

A Growing Higher Education Footprint

According to AISHE reports, India’s higher education network has expanded significantly over the decade.

The number of universities increased from 760 in 2014–15 to 1,289 in 2023–24, representing a growth of 69.6%.

The number of colleges rose from 38,498 to 48,246, an increase of 25.3%.

Standalone institutions increased from 12,276 to 15,221, registering about 24% growth.

This expansion reflects a widening institutional base and greater capacity to serve learners across the country. It has strengthened the reach of higher education, supported broader participation, and contributed to building a more accessible, diverse, and inclusive knowledge ecosystem for India’s future.

Increasing Student Enrolment: Advancing Equity and Inclusion

Higher education enrolment in India has risen steadily over the past decade, growing 31.5% from 3.42 crore students in 2014–15 to 4.50 crore in 2023–24.

The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education rose from 23.7% in 2014–15 to 29.5% in 2022–23, and further to 30% in 2023–24. This steady increase reflects growing access to and participation in higher education, supporting NEP 2020's target of raising the GER to 50% by 2035.

From 2014-15 to 2023-24, level-wise percentage increase in total enrolments was:

Ph.D 1.17 lakh to 3.43 lakh (192.89%); Post Graduate 38.53 lakh to 57.85 lakh (50.15%); Under Graduate 2.71 crore to 3.45 crore (27.27%);

Diploma 25.08 lakh to 33.15 lakh (32.22%); Certificate 1.70 lakh to 2.08 lakh (22.55%); Integrated 1.41 lakh to 5.69 lakh (301.36%).

Female enrolment in higher education has witnessed steady growth over the past decade. It grew by 42.2%, rising from 1.57 crore in 2014–15 to 2.24 crore in 2023–24, outpacing the growth in total enrolment during the decade. The number of female students enrolled in various courses in 2023-24 was:

Ph.D: 1.71 lakh; Post-Graduate: 32.53 lakh; Under Graduate: 1.71 crore

PG Diploma: 91,332; Diploma: 13.27 lakh; Certificate: 1.10 lakh, and Integrated: 2.73 lakh.

Female GER increased from 22.9% in 2014–15 to 31.2% in 2023–24, surpassing male GER (28.9%) for the seventh consecutive year.

Higher education out-turn increased from 88.28 lakh in 2014–15 to over 1.09 crore in 2023–24 a 24.06% increase. The growth reflects improved programme completion, enhanced retention, rising enrolment, and expanded institutional capacity. Supported by government initiatives, this trend highlights progress in access, equity, quality, and performance in higher education.

Higher education out-turn refers to the total number of students who pass out of higher education institutions in a given academic year.

Gender Parity Index (GPI) in higher education improved significantly, rising from 0.92 in 2014–15 to 1.08 in 2023–24. GPI for the SC category increased from 0.91 to 1.11, while ST category GPI rose from 0.81 to 1.08 during the same period.

The rising GPI points to increasing parity favoring females. The progress highlights the impact of government initiatives in promoting equity, inclusion, and balanced participation in higher education.

Gender Parity Index (GPI) The Gender Parity Index (GPI) is the ratio of GER for females to GER for males, reflecting equitable participation of females in the education system. A GPI of 1 indicates parity between the sexes. A GPI between 0 and 1 typically indicates a disparity favoring males. A GPI greater than 1 indicates a disparity favoring females.

The share of SC enrolment rose from 13.44% in 2014–15 to 15.5% in 2023–24 in total enrolment. During the same period, the share of ST enrolment increased from 4.8% to 6.4%. OBC participation climbed from 32.8% to 40.1%, registering the largest increase in enrolment share among all social categories.

The GER for SC students increased from 18.9% in 2014–15 to 27.8% in 2023–24. For the ST students, it increased from 13.5% in 2014–15 to 22.8% in 2023–24. Increasing participation of students from SC, ST and OBC categories reflects growing inclusivity in higher education.

Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) enrolment increased from 64,298 in 2014–15 to 88,816 in 2022–23, registering a growth of 38.1%. Male and female enrolment grew by 54.4% and 19.0%, respectively, during this period.

In 2023–24, 54,080 PwBD students were enrolled, including 34,080 males and 20,000 females. Higher male enrolment among PwBD points to a persistent gender imbalance in access to higher education. This suggests that improvements in access have not translated equally across genders.

Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Enrolment

Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) enrolments in higher education have increased steadily over the past decade.

Total enrolments increased from 91.5 lakh in 2014–15 to 1.02 crore in 2023–24, representing an overall increase of approximately 11.5% over the period.

The growth reflects expanding institutional capacity and sustained student interest in STEM disciplines, driven by government initiatives, digital technologies, innovation, research, and employment opportunities strengthening India's knowledge economy.

Foreign Student Enrolment in Higher Education

Foreign student enrolment rose from 42,293 in 2014–15 to 58,134 in 2023–24, an increase of approximately 37.5% over the past decade — reflecting India's growing appeal as a destination for higher learning among international students.

This points to the growing internationalisation of higher education, enhanced academic collaborations and global recognition of Indian institutions.

Faculty Growth in Higher Education

The number of teachers in higher education increased from 14.73 lakh in 2014–15 to 17.32 lakh in 2023–24, representing an overall increase of 2.59 lakh teachers, or approximately 17.6% growth during the period.

The absolute number of female teachers grew by 36.7% between 2014–15 and 2023–24, reflecting growing equity in employment opportunities for women in the sector.

In both 2022–23 and 2023–24, the share of male teachers in the total teaching workforce remained higher than that of female teachers.

In 2022-23, the share of female teachers was 44.3%. It grew marginally to 44.9% in 2023-24.

Infrastructure facilities

Between 2014–15 and 2023–24, infrastructure facilities in higher education institutions have improved considerably. Physical and digital infrastructure, green infrastructure and separate amenities for women and PwBD have been developed across institutions. In 2023–24:

94% of universities, 95% of colleges, and 91% of standalone institutions had a playground.

98% of universities, 98% of colleges, and 98% of standalone institutions had a library facility.

89% of universities, 85% of colleges, and 94% of standalone institutions had a laboratory.

In addition, most universities, colleges, and standalone institutions were also equipped with facilities such as health centres, skill development and computer centres, auditoriums, and conference halls.

Towards a Future-Ready Higher Education Ecosystem

India’s higher education sector has expanded significantly over the past decade, with growth in institutions, enrolment, faculty strength and student out-turn. Improvements in Gross Enrolment Ratio, women’s participation, gender parity, and inclusion of SC, ST and other disadvantaged groups reflect enhanced access and equity. Rising enrolment in STEM and international students indicates the strengthening of India's knowledge ecosystem. Together, these achievements highlight the impact of NEP 2020 in promoting quality, inclusion, and excellence.

The Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, chaired a review meeting on the progress of the Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U) in Chandigarh, held at the UT Guest House.

headline: National Biodiversity Authority disburses Rs. 5.68 Crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing Funds for Biodiversity Conservation
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

National Biodiversity Authority disburses Rs. 5.68 Crore in Access and Benefit-Sharing Funds for Biodiversity Conservation

30 AUG 2026 8:10PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 5.68 crore under the Access and Benefit-Sharing (ABS) mechanism arising from the utilisation of biological resources. The funds have been channelled to State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs), Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) and a national research institution, primarily in relation to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), Cucumber (Cucumis sativus) and Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), besides specified microbial and agricultural biological resources.

The largest ABS component relates to Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus), covering 139 varieties and 28 hybrids, for which the NBA has released Rs. 3.51 crore to 32 State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils. The ABS amount was received from M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd. in connection with its access to Okra.

The other major ABS components relate to Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), covering 662 varieties and 15 hybrids and Cucumber (Cucumis sativus), covering 1009 varieties and 14 hybrids. These biological resources were accessed through markets/traders by M/s. Nunhems India Pvt. Ltd., M/s. East West Seeds India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd.

The major ABS recipients among the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils are:

Sl. No. | States/UTs | Amount released (Rs.)

1. | Gujarat | 88,79,304

2. | West Bengal | 78,08,691

3. | Madhya Pradesh | 64,90,418

4. | Odisha | 59,01,641

5. | Bihar | 45,59,602

6. | Uttar Pradesh | 36,90,952

7. | Tamil Nadu | 34,11,119

8. | Andhra Pradesh | 30,58,472

9. | Chhattisgarh | 24,82,991

10. | Maharashtra | 17,57,359

11. | Others | 87,77,728

Total | 5,68,18,277

In these cases, the biological resources were accessed from markets and traders, making it not feasible to trace them to specific individual farmers, communities or a single identifiable geographic source. Accordingly, the modality recommended by the Expert Committee and approved by the Authority provides for distribution of the beneficiary share among the States and Union Territories where the concerned biological resource is cultivated.

In addition, the NBA has disbursed benefit-sharing funds to CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) – National Culture of Industrial Microorganisms, Pune, from an ABS amount received from M/s. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd., Mumbai.

The funds disbursed to the SBBs and UTBCs are to be utilised as per Section 32 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, for activities supporting the objectives of the Act. These include documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers; conservation and sustainable use of biological resources; restoration of degraded ecosystems; protection of wild relatives of cultivated plants; strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites; development and maintenance of biodiversity databases; capacity building; research; and community-oriented livelihood enhancement activities.

The funds disbursed to the research institution are to support activities including maintenance of repositories of biological resources, research and bio-survey activities, capacity building in taxonomy and conservation, and in-situ and ex-situ conservation.

With this disbursement, the total ABS amount disbursed by the NBA so far has crossed Rs. 191 crore. The disbursements reaffirm the NBA's commitment to ensuring that benefits arising from the utilisation of India's biological resources are directed towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, strengthening of institutional capacities and activities benefiting communities and other stakeholders associated with the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity.

headline: 4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

4th Tri-Services Future Warfare Course concludes in New Delhi

30 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The fourth edition of Tri-Services Future Warfare Course, conducted under the aegis of Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and coordinated by the Centre for Joint Warfare Studies (CENJOWS), concluded on August 30, 2026 after four weeks of professional military education and deliberations at Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi. The course brought together officers from the Army, Navy and Air Force, along with representatives from government organisations, academia, industry and strategic think tanks to examine emerging trends shaping the future character of warfare.

The curriculum covered geopolitical developments, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, cyber and cognitive warfare, information warfare, autonomous systems, future operations across land, maritime, air and space domains, grey-zone operations, multi-domain operations and technology-enabled warfare. The participants engaged with senior military officers, policymakers, scientists, industry leaders and subject matter experts through lectures, brainstorming sessions, scenario-building exercises, cognitive warfare simulations, field visits and participant-led presentations.

Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani interacted with the participants, seeking their views on the course and encouraging suggestions on emerging areas and additional subjects that could be incorporated in future editions to further strengthen the relevance of the programme. The course also dwelt on out-of-the-box ideas for enhancing the operational and functional efficiency of the services in an integrated ecosystem.

The valedictory programme included the presentation of certificates to the participants by the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) Air Marshal Tejinder Singh. Lt Gen SS Mahal (Retd), Managing Director Defence Research and Innovation Foundation, IIT Ropar presented 'PG Diploma in Future Warfare' to the attendees.

The fourth edition further reinforced the importance of joint learning, technological awareness, strategic foresight and operational preparedness in preparing military leaders for the evolving character of warfare. The fifth edition of the course is scheduled from November 16 till December 11, 2026.
