headline: MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow
fullText:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

MSDE in collaboration with Government of Uttar Pradesh organises PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow

From Demographic Dividend to Productive Dividend: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh Calls on Defence Industry to Partner with PM-SETU for a Viksit Bharat

Industries must go beyond CSR and take ownership of ITIs; PM-SETU is designed to bridge the gap between skilling and employment: Jayant Chaudhary, MoS (I/C), MSDE

30 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Uttar Pradesh, today organized the PM-SETU Industry Conclave in Lucknow, bringing together senior representatives from government, industry, multilateral institutions, defence public sector enterprises, sector skill councils and skilling stakeholders to deliberate on strengthening industry participation in vocational education and transforming Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into world-class centres of excellence.

The conclave was graced by of Minister of Defence Shri Rajnath Singh, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Deputy Chief Minister, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Brajesh Pathak and Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Kapil Dev Agarwal. Senior officials from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Directorate General of Training (DGT), Ministry of Defence, Government of Uttar Pradesh and industry leaders participated in the discussions.

The event witnessed participation from senior leadership of leading defence and manufacturing organizations including Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), BrahMos Aerospace, Troop Comforts Limited (TCL), Advanced Weapons and Equipment India Limited (AWEIL), Gliders India Limited (GIL), Ashok Leyland, NSDC, TCIL, PTC, along with representatives from the World Bank, industry associations and other strategic stakeholders.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasized that India's journey towards becoming a global manufacturing and technology powerhouse would be driven by the availability of highly skilled manpower. He highlighted that sectors such as defence manufacturing, aerospace, electronics, drones, robotics, precision engineering and automation are witnessing rapid technological advancements and require a workforce equipped with future-ready skills. He underscored that a strong domestic defence industrial base and a strong skilling ecosystem must grow together to support India's aspirations for self-reliance and technological leadership.

The Defence Minister highlighted Uttar Pradesh's emergence as a major hub for manufacturing and defence production, driven by the rapid growth of its industrial ecosystem and the Defence Corridor. Emphasizing the importance of stronger industry-academia linkages, he noted that collaboration between industry and training institutions is crucial to equip youth with future-ready skills and expressed confidence that such partnerships would steer the state in the right direction. He further remarked that under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath, Uttar Pradesh is witnessing transformative development across multiple sectors.

Stressing that the availability of a skilled workforce is fundamental to nation-building, he reiterated Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of converting India's demographic dividend into a productive dividend. He underscored the need to align the skilling ecosystem with industry requirements, stating that skill certificates hold value only when they lead to meaningful employment. Calling upon industries to view PM-SETU as a collaborative mission rather than merely a government scheme, he urged them to actively participate in shaping the workforce that will ultimately serve their own growth and competitiveness.

He appealed to Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) and other defence-related organizations to actively partner in the PM-SETU initiative, while also stressing the need to transform ITIs and strengthen apprenticeship opportunities. Concluding, he stated that the success of PM-SETU should be measured not by the number of machines installed, but by the employment opportunities it creates and the lives it positively impacts.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary said that PM-SETU represents a new partnership model between government, industry and training institutions. He emphasized that the initiative is designed to bridge the gap between training and employment by enabling industries to play an active role in the development, governance and operation of ITI clusters. He highlighted that the programme aims to create a future-ready workforce through industry-aligned training, modern infrastructure, apprenticeship opportunities and pathways for entrepreneurship.

Underscoring the strategic importance of the defence sector in achieving global competitiveness, he highlighted that the industry's reliance on technology and innovation makes this scheme both timely and relevant. He called upon industries to go beyond CSR initiatives and take active ownership of ITIs to strengthen the skilling landscape.

Deputy Chief Minister Shri Brajesh Pathak assured full support to participating industries and emphasized the government's continued focus on strengthening the skilling ecosystem as a key driver towards realizing the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

Shri Kapil Dev Agrawal, Minister of State (Independent Charge), Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said that Uttar Pradesh is committed to strengthening its skilling ecosystem to meet the needs of a rapidly expanding industrial and manufacturing base. Referring to the state's extensive network of government ITIs and the identification of eight PM-SETU clusters in Uttar Pradesh, he noted that the initiative provides a unique opportunity to align vocational training with industry requirements and emerging technologies.

Welcoming the participants, Shri Dilip Kumar, Director General -Training, highlighted the transformational potential of PM-SETU in creating a deeper and more structured engagement between industry and the skilling ecosystem. He noted that the initiative empowers Anchor Industry Partners (AIPs) to actively contribute to the growth and modernization of ITI clusters, ensuring direct alignment between institutional outcomes and industry requirements.

Dr. Hari Om, Principal Secretary, Vocational Education, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the significant opportunities the state offers for strengthening the skilling ecosystem and called upon industry leaders to play an active role in supporting these efforts. Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), presented an insightful overview of PM-SETU, helping the audience gain a deeper understanding of the program and its vision.

Addressing the audience, Shri Vijay Karan Anand, Chief Executive Officer, Invest UP, underscored the far-reaching benefits of the scheme and called upon officials and stakeholders to proactively participate in its rollout. He emphasized the importance of strong partnerships in realizing the scheme's vision and maximizing its impact across the state.

Representatives from defence public sector undertakings and strategic industries highlighted the growing demand for skilled technicians in areas such as aerospace systems, shipbuilding, electronics manufacturing, precision engineering, defence production, advanced welding, mechatronics and drone technologies. Industry participants reiterated their commitment to partnering with government to create sustainable talent pipelines through industry-led skilling models.

Under the PM-SETU Scheme, cluster projects comprising one Hub ITI and four Spoke ITIs can attract investments of up to ₹241 crore, supported through a funding pattern of 50% from the Government of India, 33% from State Governments and 17% from Industry Partners. Unlike traditional partnership models, the proposed Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) structure provides 51% ownership to Anchor Industry Partners, while the Centre and State Governments hold 24.5% ownership each, ensuring meaningful industry leadership in cluster development and operations. In UP so far, 32 ITIs in 8 Clusters have already been identified out of which seven are still open for collaboration.

The conclave was informed that approved Industry Partnership proposals under PM-SETU currently represent more than ₹1,500 crore of committed industry-led investment across seven clusters in five states, with several additional proposals under consideration.

During the event, NSDC and the Lucknow Cantonment Board signed an MoU to establish Shaurya Academy, a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at preparing youth for careers in the Armed Forces, Police, and other uniformed services.

headline: Joint Statement during the State Visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Joint Statement during the State Visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Uzbekistan

30 AUG 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

At the invitation of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, His Excellency Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the Prime Minister of the Republic of India, His Excellency Mr. Narendra Modi, paid a State Visit to the Republic of Uzbekistan from 29 to 30 August 2026.

President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks in a warm, friendly and constructive atmosphere. The Leaders conducted a comprehensive review of the current state and future prospects of the Uzbekistan-India bilateral relations, exchanged views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, and identified priority areas for further practical cooperation.

The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the strong level of collaboration between the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Republic of India. They noted that the relationship is firmly anchored in longstanding bonds of friendship, as well as deep historical and cultural affinities between the two nations. Reaffirming their shared resolve, the Leaders underscored their commitment to further deepening bilateral ties and elevating cooperation to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership that advances the core interests of both nations.

The Leaders welcomed the close alignment of their positions and the growing importance of Central Asia. Amid a complex geopolitical situation, they stressed the need for a free, open and rules-based international order. Building on their multilateral cooperation, Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and bilateral agreements, they reaffirmed their commitment to long-term, mutually beneficial cooperation for both peoples and future generations, agreeing to deepen political dialogue and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership across trade, economy and investment, transport connectivity, digital transformation (IT, AI, space, cybersecurity), energy transition, critical minerals, food security, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and education.

Political, Parliamentary and Security Cooperation

The Leaders underscored the importance of maintaining regular and trust-based dialogue at leadership and institutional levels and agreed to continue the exchange of visits and contacts in both the bilateral format and on the margins of international events.

The Leaders agreed to establish Foreign Ministers led mechanism to provide high level coordination and oversight of the implementation of the agreements and arrangements reached between the two countries, as well as to facilitate the timely realisation of priority bilateral initiatives and projects.

The Leaders acknowledged the growing role of parliamentary diplomacy and welcomed the intensification of contacts between the chambers of the Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Parliament of the Republic of India, including cooperation between parliamentary friendship groups and interaction within international inter-parliamentary organizations.

The Leaders underscored the importance of further strengthening the legal framework of bilateral cooperation across various fields. They emphasized the need for a comprehensive review of the existing bilateral legal instruments to ensure that they fully reflect the current priorities of bilateral engagement and agreed to work jointly on modernizing the treaty framework in line with present-day realities.

The Leaders unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, reiterated zero tolerance approach to terrorism and rejected justification of terrorism on any ground whatsoever. Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and for disrupting terrorism financing networks, safe havens and infrastructure. Leaders stressed that those responsible for terrorism should be held accountable and their perpetrators, their backers, facilitators and affiliates should be brought to justice. The Leaders stressed the importance of strengthening cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence-sharing, and combating violent extremism, and illicit drug trafficking, organized crime, and cyber threats. The Leaders reaffirmed the importance of continued cooperation under the Joint Working Group on Counter Terrorism.

The Leaders appreciated the growing cooperation and close coordination between the defence and security agencies of Uzbekistan and India, including through regular exchanges, institutional mechanisms, capacity-building and joint activities, and expressed their commitment to further strengthen such cooperation in addressing shared security challenges. The Leaders expressed satisfaction with the activities of the Joint Working Group on Military Cooperation, wherein new avenues of cooperation in the defence industrial domain are being explored. They welcomed the successful conduct of Uzbekistan – India Joint Military Exercise “Dustlik”, the latest of which was held in Namangan Region, Uzbekistan, in April 2026.

The Leaders highly appreciated the progress achieved in regional cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening engagement within Central Asia – India format at the level of Heads of States and other levels. The Leaders also underscored the importance of continuing regular consultations on regional issues.

Trade, Economic and Investment Cooperation

The Leaders welcomed the strong economic partnership between Uzbekistan and India and noted the considerable untapped potential for further expanding bilateral trade and investment.

The Leaders agreed on the importance of enhancing and diversifying bilateral trade by identifying and harnessing new opportunities. They underscored that the rapidly growing number of Indian companies operating in Uzbekistan reflect the significant potential for further expanding economic cooperation.

Both sides agreed to undertake joint measures to broaden the range of goods traded between the two countries, remove non tariff barriers, and promote industrial cooperation with a view to further increasing bilateral trade turnover. They decided to create a Joint Working Group to address non tariff issues and investment barriers, with a particular focus on key sectors of bilateral trade.

Both sides expressed their interest in strengthening cooperation in the fields of e-commerce, the digitalization of trade procedures, and the introduction of digital platforms to support small and medium-sized enterprises and facilitate bilateral trade.

The Uzbek side appreciated the support of the Indian side on accession of the Republic of Uzbekistan at WTO. Both sides agreed to work together to preserve and protect the multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core, especially for the interests of the developing countries.

Both sides agreed to support efforts aimed at strengthening manufacturing and export capacities, to promote dialogue among regulators and explore mutual recognition arrangements to facilitate faster and greater market access in each others’ markets.

The Leaders highly appreciated the outcomes of the meeting of the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific and Technical Cooperation and the Uzbekistan – India Business Forums, held in June 2026 on the sidelines of the Tashkent International Investment Forum and in August 2026 in New Delhi, noting their significant contribution to the further expansion of trade, economic and investment cooperation between the two countries.

The Leaders agreed to promote collaboration between the Uzbek and the Indian companies, leverage the complementarities between the two economies and strengthen connectivity between their value-added supply chains..

Both sides acknowledged the great potential of bilateral trade in Electrical items, Engineering products, Automobiles and Pharma sectors and agreed to closer business-to-business tie up in these sectors.

The Leaders agreed to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities and establish an institutional mechanism to address investors' concerns and facilitate ease of doing business.

Both sides agreed to explore enhanced cooperation between the Investment Promotion Agency of Uzbekistan and Invest India to identify and promote mutually beneficial investment opportunities, including through joint business forums, roadshows, investment seminars and stakeholder’s interaction, with a view to facilitating greater two way investment flows and strengthening business-to-business linkages.

The two Leaders expressed satisfaction at the steady growth of bilateral trade and reaffirmed their resolve to further expand and diversify trade, with the aim of building a stronger trade relationship. Recalling the conclusion of the Joint Feasibility Study on Uzbekistan-India Preferential Trade Agreement, the Leaders directed the relevant Ministries to explore the next steps on a time bound basis.

Energy, Natural Resources and Supply Chains

The Leaders welcomed the discussions on advancing cooperation in the fields of renewable energy, modernization of energy infrastructure, and the implementation of prospective investment projects.

The Leaders agreed to explore for cooperation in the fields of geology, mining, nuclear energy, industrial cooperation, and critical & strategic minerals, including projects for the processing of mineral resources, production of value- added products and recycling initiatives. They also expressed interest in encouraging Indian companies to participate in the development of prospective mineral deposits in Uzbekistan and Uzbek enterprises for joint collaboration in India. The Leaders expressed interest in extended cooperation in peaceful uses of nuclear energy.

The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in the field of critical minerals through the implementation of joint projects in geological exploration, mining, mineral processing, and the development of integrated value chains.

The Leaders agreed to cooperate in the development of agricultural value chains, strengthening export capabilities, and enhancing the technical capacity of agriculture and livestock sectors.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in agriculture and food security, with a particular focus on innovation and resource-efficient technologies. They also agreed to continue exchanges in the field of agricultural science and to make effective use of multilateral and regional platforms to promote the development of modern and sustainable agriculture across the region. The Leaders agreed to facilitate bilateral trade in agricultural products.

The Leaders supported the expansion of cooperation between research institutions and enterprises in enhancing agricultural productivity, as well as in the conservation and sustainable utilization of plant genetic resources.

Transport, Logistics and Connectivity

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to continuing joint efforts to enhance transport and logistics connectivity between Uzbekistan and India through the development of multimodal transport routes and logistics corridors, creating favourable conditions for the seamless movement of goods.

The Leaders reaffirmed their intention to continue cooperation aimed at restoring freight transportation in order to reduce transportation costs.

The Leaders expressed their intention to expand cooperation between the relevant authorities through the exchange of expertise in road construction using advanced technologies and to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects on the reconstruction and modernization of road infrastructure.

The Leaders recognized the importance of developing environmentally friendly and energy-efficient solutions for Uzbekistan’s public transport sector and agreed to explore opportunities for implementing joint projects in this field.

Digital Technologies, Innovation and Space Cooperation

The Leaders welcomed the successful operation of the first IT Park in Tashkent, established in 2019 based on the Indian model with the active support of the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), and agreed to further expand partnerships among technology parks, companies, startups, and educational institutions of the two countries.

The Leaders welcomed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation in the fields of high technologies and digital transformation, as well as the implementation of the understandings reached in February 2026 on the margins of the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi.

The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the development and advancement of safe, secure, and trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI) systems, including through the exchange of experience and best practices, with a view to harnessing AI’s potential to promote sustainable economic growth, innovation-driven development, and the effective resolution of societal challenges.

The Leaders reaffirmed their interest in further expanding practical cooperation in the exploration and peaceful uses of outer space, including in space applications, the exchange of scientific data, and capacity-building through joint workshops and training.

Education, Human Resource Development, Healthcare, Culture, Sports and Tourism

The Leaders recognised the valuable contribution of Indian students to strengthening the longstanding people-to-people ties between Uzbekistan and India.

The Leaders welcomed the continued expansion of India studies in Uzbekistan and supported the expansion of Uzbek studies in India.

The Leaders shared the view of strengthening cooperation in human resource development, which serves as an important bridge between Uzbekistan and India, including through the implementation of joint research programmes and academic cooperation initiatives.

The Leaders appreciated the longstanding and mutually beneficial partnership in capacity building and human resource development, particularly in the fields of medicine, pharmaceuticals, chemistry, nanotechnology and biotechnology. Over the years, more than 2,700 Uzbek nationals have participated in the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme, while more than 400 Uzbek students have been selected under ICCR scholarships, including scholarships under AYUSH. In this context, Uzbek side welcomed the announcement of Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi Language in Uzbekistan. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to further promote cooperation in human resource development under the ITEC Programme.

Uzbekistan and India share the aspiration of leaving a greener and healthier planet for future generations, as reflected in Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiatives. Building on this shared commitment, India and Uzbekistan will cooperate in the greening and ecological rehabilitation of the Aral Sea region. These rehabilitation efforts of US $1 million, including the provision of necessary technical support, will be undertaken under India’s Grant-in-Aid framework.

The Leaders agreed to expand cooperation in strengthening public health systems, including in the fields of biomedical research and medical innovation, by leveraging each other’s strengths to develop new treatments and therapies through advanced scientific research.

The Leaders highly appreciated the growing cooperation in the pharmaceutical sector and underscored the significant potential of the Tashkent Pharma Park Innovative Scientific and Industrial Pharmaceutical Cluster as an effective platform for implementing joint projects, attracting investment in modern pharmaceutical manufacturing, localizing production, facilitating technology transfer, and developing a highly skilled workforce. The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to promoting closer cooperation between the relevant institutions and pharmaceutical companies of the two countries.

The Leaders expressed their support for the establishment in Uzbekistan, in cooperation with Indian companies, of new medical centres and laboratories, as well as research institutions and joint pharmaceutical manufacturing enterprises.

Recognizing the centuries-old historical ties, shared cultural and civilizational heritage, and longstanding traditions of mutual respect between the peoples of Uzbekistan and India, the Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cultural and humanitarian cooperation through the organization of cultural days, festivals, exhibitions, tours by artistic ensembles, and by strengthening direct links between the cultural institutions of the two countries. Both Leaders welcomed the signing of the Cultural Exchange Program from 2026-2030 and the Uzbekistan-India cooperation in the Field of Archives.

The Leaders underscored the importance of cooperation in the preservation, study, restoration and promotion of World Heritage sites and expressed their interest in expanding collaboration among relevant research institutions, museums and restoration centres, including in the digitalization of cultural heritage sites, the creation of three-dimensional (3D) models of archaeological artefacts, and the application of advanced technologies for their conservation. In this regard, both Leaders appreciated the Letter of Intent signed on the conservation and restoration of ancient Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Karatepa.

The Leaders agreed to strengthen cooperation in the field of sports, including through the exchange of experience in athlete preparation and coach training in such disciplines as badminton, archery and chess.

The Leaders noted with satisfaction the role of yoga in promoting healthy lifestyles and strengthening people-to-people ties, and emphasised the significance of the International Day of Yoga on 21 June. The Leaders welcomed cooperation between the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan and India's Ministry of AYUSH on instructor training and also Uzbekistan's participation in international Yogasana competitions. The Leaders reaffirmed their readiness to continue supporting the promotion and development of yoga in Uzbekistan with the participation of leading Indian experts. The Leaders also welcomed the conclusion of the MoU for cooperation in traditional medicines.

International Cooperation

Both Leaders reaffirmed that the United Nations must play a central role in maintaining global peace and security. They agreed to strengthen their cooperation, including through mutual support, in the United Nations and other international and regional organizations.

Both Leaders called for comprehensive reform of the UN, including Security Council, to reflect contemporary global realities and to make it more representative, effective and efficient in dealing with issues of international peace and security. Uzbekistan reaffirmed its support to India’s candidature for permanent membership of the UN Security Council.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening coordination in international fora with a view to advancing the common interests of the countries of the Global South.

The Leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), recognizing it as an important platform for enhancing mutual trust, promoting regional peace, security and stability, and expanding cooperation in trade and economic affairs, investment, and cultural and humanitarian exchanges.

President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi on India’s Chairship of BRICS in 2026 and wished him every success in hosting the BRICS Summit.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed confidence in Uzbekistan’s successful Chairship of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) for the period 2027-2030 and reaffirmed India’s readiness to continue supporting the Movement as its founding member.

Both Leaders noted the important role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) and the International Solar Alliance (ISA), as platforms for advancing global cooperation in their respective fields. The Indian side welcomed Uzbek side’s interest in joining these frameworks and conveyed its readiness to actively pursue the necessary consultations and processes towards their accession.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his sincere gratitude to the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev, as well as to the Government and the people of Uzbekistan, for the warm welcome and gracious hospitality extended to him during the visit.

Prime Minister of India invited the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan to pay a return visit to India. The dates will be decided through diplomatic channels.

headline: Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan

30 AUG 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

As part of his State Visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today held official talks with the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev. On arrival at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace, Prime Minister was warmly received by President Mirziyoyev and accorded a ceremonial welcome. He conveyed his warmest wishes to Uzbekistan on the occasion of their 35th anniversary of Independence.

The two leaders held wide-ranging and substantive discussions in delegation level format on the entire gamut of the bilateral strategic partnership, including trade and investment, innovation and start-up, digital public infrastructure and UPI, defence and security, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, critical minerals, agriculture, education, tourism, agriculture, space and people-to-people exchanges. Prime Minister appreciated the progress made in the long-term arrangement for supply of Uranium from Uzbekistan to India and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening cooperation in critical minerals. Reflecting the depth and salience of the relationship, they decided to elevate the bilateral Strategic Partnership to the level of Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They also agreed to set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030 and in this regard called for hosting a Business Summit to deepen economic and investment ties. To take forward the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in a meaningful manner, the two leaders agreed to set up a Foreign Ministers led mechanism and raise the Inter-Governmental Commission to the ministerial level.

The leaders noted that ancient civilizational linkages and contemporary people-to-people ties continue to add vitality to the partnership. In this regard, Prime Minister appreciated the popularity of Yoga in Uzbekistan. Earlier in the day, he viewed a Yoga Session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan. To commemorate the 60th anniversary of the passing of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Prime Minister Modi announced the Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students . Recognising the convergence between Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” green initiative and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, Prime Minister Modi announced India’s partnership with Uzbekistan in the ongoing environmental rehabilitation efforts in the Aral Sea region with a grant of USD 1 million for the project. The two leaders also jointly planted a tree in the Palace garden.

Following the talks, the two sides witnessed the exchange of MoUs and agreements covering a wide range of areas, including culture, higher education and research, capacity building, archives, economic collaboration, environment, tourism, mining, ayurveda and sister-state relations. A Letter of Intent for the restoration of the Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa in Uzbekistan was concluded. An MoU for the establishment of an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies was also finalised. The full list of MoUs and agreements can be accessed here.

President Mirziyoyev hosted a banquet lunch in honour of Prime Minister. Prime Minister thanked President Mirziyoyev for his gracious hospitality and invited him to visit India.
